videos.title: Stop Watching AI Slop Build These Projects Instead
videos.description:
If your feed looks anything like mine right now, it is full of AI content. And a lot of it is the same thing recycled over and over with a new thumbnail.
So here's what I'd actually build instead of watching another top 10 AI tools video:

Build a personal finance tracker that reads your actual statements and automatically categorizes your spending. You'll use it every month.
Build an email agent that triages your inbox and drafts responses for the ones that follow a pattern. You'll feel the time savings immediately.
Build a research tool that takes a topic, pulls sources, and gives you a summary you can actually trust. Every time you need to learn something new, it's already there.

The difference between people who are getting better at AI and people who just know a lot about AI is the building. That's it. That's the whole gap.

Pick one. Start today.

videos.title: Improve Flexibility with Research-Supported Stretching Protocols | Huberman Lab Essentials
videos.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, I explain the biology of flexibility and discuss the organ systems that shape range of motion and limb flexibility. I also discuss different types of stretching, which methods are most effective, and practical tools for timing stretching relative to exercise. Finally, I provide specific protocols for how intensely and how often to stretch to maximize flexibility, support exercise performance, and offset age-related losses of flexibility.

videos.title: The agent line keeps going up—and you need to identify what's below it.
videos.description: Many interactions, decisions, and directions that feel like they need human judgment actually fit "below the agent line." If you took the information from a meeting and gave it to an agent, would it solve the same problem? Increasingly, the answer is yes. The best teams push this line higher by building smart skills and integrations that expand what agents can handle autonomously.
